He also played a role in the 1621-1623 papal election, which saw the ascension of Pope Gregory XV, and was part of the conclave that elected Pope Urban VIII's successor, Pope Innocent X, in 1623-1625. Sfondrati's influence extended beyond the Vatican, as he was involved in diplomatic efforts with European powers, including the Holy Roman Empire and the French monarchy. His connections to the Sfondrati family also led to his involvement in the Catholic Counter-Reformation, which aimed to suppress Protestantism in Europe. The cardinal's legacy is a testament to the enduring power of the Catholic Church, which continues to shape the lives of millions of people around the world.
